blocks.content: A Pod you create by hand is not managed by anything. If its node dies, the Pod dies with it and nothing brings it back.

blocks.title: Use a controller
blocks.content: Create a Deployment instead. It owns a ReplicaSet, which keeps the number of Pods you asked for alive across node failures and rollouts.

# Replaces a failed Pod automatically
kubectl create deployment web --image=nginx:1.27

# Scale it
kubectl scale deployment/web --replicas=3

blocks.title: When a bare Pod is fine
blocks.content: Debugging. `kubectl run -it --rm debug --image=busybox` gives you a throwaway shell in the cluster, and you want it gone when you exit.
